metadata.case_name: TONG YUK TAI v. CHEW SOOI KUEN

plaintiff.occupation_before: Majority owner of a shop selling, inter alia, second-hand prestigious watches; watch technician of the shop receiving a monthly salary

injuries.description: soft tissue injury to the neck
source: Tong was found to have sustained soft tissue injury to the neck which should be due to the Accident and his current neck impairment would persist.
After the Accident, Tong attended the A&E Department of of Pok Oi Hospital and was found to have mild tenderness over the right side of his neck.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of muscle, fascia or tendon at neck level

manifestations.description: mild tenderness over the right side of his neck
right neck muscle swelling with tenderness
reduced range of motion of the neck
neck pain being aggravated by bending the neck or the neck staying immobile for 15 minutes
on-and-off pin prick sensation over right little finger
increased neck pain when lifting heavy objects
waken up 4 to 5 times a week due to neck pain

treatments_received.treatment: A&E treatment at Pok Oi Hospital
source: After the Accident, Tong attended the A&E Department of of Pok Oi Hospital and was found to have mild tenderness over the right side of his neck. He was treated and discharged.

treatments_received.treatment: Consultation and treatment by family doctor Dr Chan (analgesic, anti-inflammatory drug and hypnotic) with sick leave
source: Tong sought treatment from his family doctor Dr Chan Ka Lung ("Dr Chan") for about 25 times from 15 June 2012 to 31 May 2013. Physical examination of Tong by Dr Chan revealed right neck muscle swelling with tenderness. Tong was treated with analgesic, anti-inflammatory drug and hypnotic and discharged with sick leave.
Reportedly, Tong further received physiotherapy treatment by an acquaintance for 10 times.

treatments_received.treatment: Conservative treatment (medication and physiotherapy) by orthopaedic surgeon Dr Au
source: Due to persistent neck pain, Tong was subsequently referred by Dr Chan to an orthopaedic surgeon Dr Au Kin Ming ("Dr Au") for further treatment. Physical examination on 1 November 2012 revealed tenderness of right neck muscle and reduced range of motion of the neck. Tong also reported numbness of his right hand over the ulnar side. Conservative treatment with medication and physiotherapy were suggested and sick leave was granted.

treatments_future.treatment: No further treatment except symptomatic one
source: Tong did not need further treatment except symptomatic one.

comparable_cases.injury_description: the plaintiff, aged 37, suffered whiplash injury to the neck resulting in neck pain and stiffness ... persistent numbness over the right upper back, neck pain, on and off right arm numbness and increasing left shoulder pain after prolonged driving
